A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hyperfitting research and contain readable main text, Tables 1–8, Figures 1–11, and Appendices A–C. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original human evaluations, text-generation experiments, data-influence analyses, and ImageGPT results, plus instruction-tuned model and MMLU/GLUE evaluations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–7 and Appendices A–C, including human-preference measurements and downstream benchmark scores.

M1.justification: The next-token hyperfitting procedure, model components, greedy generation, and citation-blocking procedure remain unchanged. The image and instruction-tuned model applications are also retained without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use fiction, Wikipedia, and BBC News for text generation, CIFAR-10 for image generation, and MMLU/GLUE for downstream evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Top-P baselines for TinyLlama, DeepSeek, and Llama 3.1 alongside the same original-model and citation-blocking comparisons. The ImageGPT and appendix base/chat comparison sets are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, the 300-context human evaluation, continuation lengths, decoding parameters, and metrics are unchanged. Appendices A–B retain the same annotation, image-generation, and MMLU/GLUE protocols.

E4.justification: Both retain the data-order, data-type, and sample-quantity analyses in Section 6, overlap and citation-blocking analyses, TTR/human-preference analysis, and Appendix C examples. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: The model-instance counts in Section 3 and fixed-seed information for the data-order experiment in Section 6.1 are unchanged. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8, plotted results, and qualitative examples match across versions, including the appendix MMLU/GLUE scores and generated texts. No result entries or findings are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions and the reasoning about probability, entropy, and token ranks remain unchanged. Adding 'Hypothesis' to the Section 7.3 heading introduces no new formal assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about generation improvements, sharpened predictions, limited training-data copying, and applicability to image generation. The wording edits do not alter their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of perplexity, data influence, and generalization, together with the stated limitations and open questions, are unchanged. Section 7.3's revised heading restates the hypothesis status already explicit in v1.

D1.justification: The introduction adds a project GitHub pointer stating that skeleton code and models are available. This supplies access information absent from v1; implementation details and hyperparameters are otherwise unchanged. The PDFs do not verify the linked contents.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography, and positioning relative to grokking, double descent, and existing generation methods are unchanged. The new acknowledgements and review-page link do not introduce additional prior research.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations, corrects 'outperform' to 'outperforms' in the abstract, adds 'Hypothesis' to the Section 7.3 heading, and adds resource and acknowledgement text. The narrative and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds ICLR 2025 running headers, reformats the author/affiliation block, and places acknowledgements on page 10, with limited local text reflow. All figures and tables retain their design, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: The added code/model pointer modestly improves reproducibility documentation, while the Section 7.3 heading makes the existing hypothesis status clearer. Scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited; the PDFs cannot establish the linked resources' completeness.
